scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: a blocked waterway you could fix in about ten minutes if all sides were willing; what's harder to fix is the destruction of refineries
lines.note: ranks the two causes: the strait is reversible, refineries are not

lines.quote: 825 refineries on the planet for 8.3 billion people; a big one costs $25 billion and takes more than ten years to build
lines.note: sizes the choke — the lowest-Dia line in the tape
lines.zWhy: scarcity of the plant is the bite's precondition

lines.quote: seven refineries in the Persian Gulf hit so far in this war — if you're wondering why diesel is $6.50 nationally, it's because of that; and Russia, which refines about 7% of the world's diesel
lines.note: the crunch dated and sourced, by his count

lines.quote: why would Ukraine be hitting Russian refineries — apparently 60% of Russia's refinery capacity has been hit
lines.note: a number stated; Weichert gives 45% at 59:56 — the tape disagrees with itself
lines.zWhy: capacity removed is supply removed: bites

lines.quote: Nord Stream was the largest man-made CO2 emission in history and the Sierra Club didn't say a word
lines.note: the climate frame enters; the object leaves

lines.quote: when you destroy refineries you hike the price of diesel beyond what most people can pay — $6.50 for the energy source that gets goods from manufacturer to warehouse to home
lines.note: THE BITE, stated: the crunch as a cost people cannot pay, not a cost that passes

lines.quote: destroying the world's refining capacity achieves the same effect as the climate agenda — fewer people, by starvation or by having fewer kids
lines.note: the destruction mode: intent read off effect; the highest-Dia line
lines.zWhy: a bite so total it is read as the design

lines.quote: $6.50 diesel isn't an ancillary byproduct of this war; it's the whole point. The point of a system is what it does
lines.note: THE THESIS: the crunch as the object's purpose. The inversion in one sentence
lines.zWhy: the crunch believed to bite, and to be meant to

lines.quote: China liquefies coal into diesel; China is fine, we're not; Europe is shafted
lines.note: a real mechanism (coal-to-liquids) carrying a frame (the beneficiary)

lines.quote: Trump understands commodities — diesel is the liquid inside trucks that keeps the global economy going; without it, it grinds to a halt
lines.note: the model: diesel as the economy's working fluid; bite by definition

lines.quote: Brent has gone over 100 but it's not 300; crude has stayed pretty reasonable — it's the refined products you've got to worry about, and diesel in particular, because they advertise the price at your gas station
lines.note: THE CRACK, in a populist's words: crude reasonable, product not — Kang's 18:36 finding, from the other corner

lines.quote: Trump asked what's going on with diesel and they told him it's not the Middle East, it's the Ukrainians smacking Russian refineries — Russia is number two in the world for diesel
lines.note: dates the attribution (September); 'smacking' the one vehicle word
lines.zWhy: the cause located; the shortage assumed

lines.quote: Mr. Zelensky has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia — he's causing a shortage of diesel fuel; this isn't done by the Middle East; don't hit diesel fuel, because that's hurting the world
lines.note: constitutive (09-20): the principal names the crunch as a shortage and locates its cause — the predecessor statement to the 10-09 deal

lines.quote: that's last Sunday — a pretty smart thing to say; he's identified one of the main causes of the problem
lines.note: RP crediting the instrument, briefly
lines.zWhy: agrees the shortage is real and caused

lines.quote: the only reason it continues is the Trump administration giving the Ukrainians targeting information through its intel agencies
lines.note: the agency frame; right domain (who decides), wrong plane (the crunch)

lines.quote: people are going to have to pay some extra gas … and when the war ends your gas prices are going to drop to a level they were before, maybe even lower
lines.note: constitutive (09-18): the principal reads the crunch as a price, temporary — the pass-through side. Two statements five days apart read Z opposite ways

lines.quote: a week after Trump publicly tells Zelensky not to bomb Russian refineries, Zelensky bombs the refinery ten miles from Moscow
lines.note: the record: the request not honored (BBC, ≈09-22); 'gives Trump the finger' is the vehicle, left out of the reduction
lines.zWhy: supply removed after the request: bites harder

lines.quote: energy prices so high that you get 15-minute cities and people eating bugs
lines.note: the bite as a design
lines.zWhy: the bite as the intended end state

lines.quote: congratulations — they need to increase these strikes; it's the only way to put pressure on Putin
lines.note: the quoted institutional voice (CNN) reads the strikes as leverage; the crunch unmentioned — vacancy on the object, by a reader inside the tape
lines.zWhy: more strikes, more removed supply; the crunch not his subject

lines.quote: that is a retired four-star admiral, head of NATO under Obama, a Carlyle partner, chairman of the Rockefeller Foundation — the physical embodiment of the actual rulers
lines.note: the person as the object

lines.quote: the point of this exercise is to dethrone the United States, impoverish the US and Europe, and make way for China
lines.note: the thesis restated as intent — the highest-Dia line

lines.quote: we haven't built a new refinery since the late 1970s; ours were designed for heavy sour crude; we drill light sweet and export it, and import heavy sour from Mexico and Canada — caviar out, quarter-pounder in
lines.note: the US plumbing, correctly: configuration, not count

lines.quote: we max out our refining capacity for short-term profit; China has spare capacity, 30% in the sanctioned Shandong teapots, a 1.6–1.8 billion-barrel reserve
lines.note: the comparison, with numbers — some verifiable
lines.zWhy: no slack means a shock bites

lines.quote: 45% of Russia's refining capacity has been taken offline as of this month; the United States is already at capacity
lines.note: the number, dated (September) — against Carlson's 60% at 6:26

lines.quote: we're creating a situation where China has a lot of cards — processing dominance, as with rare earths
lines.note: the frame with a mechanism inside it
lines.zWhy: leverage presumes the West is short

lines.quote: who's making that decision? I think it's the CIA — the Ukraine war is being run out of Langley
lines.note: the agency frame again

lines.quote: the Russians are advancing on the eastern front; two of the four fortress cities taken
lines.note: the war's record; no claim on the crunch
